title: Hatchet, the Memphis pianist of the 1920s
summary: Interviewer asks about a pianist called Hatchet who accompanied a singer in 1920s Memphis; Sunnyland Slim describes him as a tall piano player and talks about Memphis associates.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: There was a Hatchet who made a record accompaniment to a vocal by Kaiser Clifton in Memphis.
In Memphis in the 20s. It must have been him.
No, Hatchet is nobody. In Memphis in the 20s.

Yeah, that's what he played here in the 20s. That was a ball piano. Him and Willie Bloom was the... You stay here with Memphis Femme at the Grimer? You know what I'm saying? You didn't hear that? No. My name is Memphis Femme. Come in the Grimer. You know why he got that in Willie Bloom? He got that J. No Sola. He got two Js in the Old Sola. Every time I go down, he trying to get the help.
He got that in Burmese, man, that woman had him alive.

Yeah, you know, and then kill him that boy up there. I bought his boy up there. He was coming to Cairo to see me. And I take his car and go over the miles to this big guy in Memphis. He owned all that property. He didn't buy him two cases, get him two cases of whiskey, get him dead. Willie would put me ten or fifteen dollars. The man was wrecking the money after this woman dead. Everything turned over to him.
Excuse me, I want to go back to that Hatchet. I'm interested in him. There was only one Hatchet in Memphis, as far as you know. All of a Hatchet in Memphis.
The fat, brown-skinned hair. His stomach wasn't big as brother. He was taller than brother. Oh, yes. Hatchet was a tall piano player.
Eddie Boyd knew also a Hatchet, and that one was called... That same Hatchet did Eddie Boyd know.

Edward Hatchet. Because Eddie Boyd wasn't playing nothing then, when that Hatchet was... He was trying to play. I'm going to tell you who he was running with. Don't you know, the boy would play a drum, Willa Hood? Huh? Well he did. I used to miss around with his old lady, him. Willa Hood. Oh, we missed another piano player too. Holston the Inn, drummer. Holston. Holston's a good piano player. A good old piano player.
